name: Kaplan Preference Matrix
citation: Kaplan, R. & Kaplan, S. (1989). The experience of nature: A psychological perspective. Cambridge University Press.

constructs.description: Low aggregate PE → fluency → preference. Maps to visual statistics + rapid gist + processing fluency.
Moderate PE → engagement on inverted-U. Maps to visual rhythm + novelty dopamine.
Low spatial PE → confident cognitive mapping. Maps to spatial integration + landmarks.
Anticipated PE reduction → dopaminergic wanting. Promenade sequencing + novelty anticipation + isovist control + safety gate.

schema_gaps: Semantic coherence not fully captured by visual statistics alone
irreducible_residual.narrative: The Kaplan Matrix may BE Predictive Processing applied to environmental scenes. Each variable maps to a specific region of the PE landscape — Coherence to fluency zone, Complexity to engagement zone, Legibility to spatial confidence zone, Mystery to anticipated-PE-reduction reward zone. The irreducible residuals — semantic coherence, expertise-dependent optima, mystery-danger interaction — all require IE-DPT.

key_references: Kaplan, R. & Kaplan, S. (1989). The experience of nature. Cambridge University Press.
Kaplan, S. (1987). Aesthetics, affect, and cognition. Environ. Behav., 19(1), 3-32.

variables.Mystery: Promise of information if one goes deeper (inferred exploration)

predictions: Mystery strongest single predictor of preference (r ≈ 0.35)
Coherence and complexity jointly predict 40-55% of landscape preference
